scopeNote: Weighted geographic assessment of the recreational marine markets considered by Workstream A. Criteria and weights were frozen before any region was scored; the weighted score measures absolute attractiveness, while the recommendation field adds a separately labelled sequencing overlay.
scoringScale: Each criterion is scored 1-5. Weighted score = sum(score x weight), range 1.00-5.00. Normalised score = weighted / 5 x 100. Scores are analyst judgements anchored to the cited claims; they are not measurements and carry the confidence of their weakest supporting claim.

baseDensity.definition: Documented recreational berth capacity and vessel population available in the region.
baseDensity.rationale: Installation-heavy hardware needs a physically present installed base; this is the strongest single determinant of reachable demand and the criterion with the best available evidence.

demandMomentum.definition: Direction of new recreational registrations in the most recent published year (2025 vs 2024).
demandMomentum.rationale: New owners are the most likely equipment buyers; momentum signals a growing rather than contracting addressable pool. Weighted below base because a one-year change on a small provincial base is noisy.

addressableMix.definition: Plausible share of craft in the 6-16 m band where navigation, gateway and monitoring electronics are economically sensible.
addressableMix.rationale: Electronics relevance is a hard eligibility filter. Scored conservatively because no regional length distribution exists; the national registration mix is used as a proxy.

commercialOperators.definition: Presence of charter, rental, school or small-professional operators that could buy MAREA FLEET.
commercialOperators.rationale: The only segment with a plausible recurring per-vessel revenue model that does not depend on individual owner spending.

seasonalityWindow.definition: Length and intensity of the operating season, including documented peak occupancy.
seasonalityWindow.rationale: Installation, commissioning and service capacity are consumed in a short window; a long shoulder season raises the number of installs a partner can complete.

channelEcosystem.definition: Documented presence of installers, refit yards and chandlery able to sell and support hardware.
channelEcosystem.rationale: Hardware cannot be sold without competent local installation; evidence is weak (two individual provider pages), so the weight is deliberately limited.

evidenceQuality.definition: Availability and robustness of region-specific published data for the other six criteria.
evidenceQuality.rationale: A market that cannot be evidenced cannot be planned; this is a decision-risk criterion, kept modest so it never dominates market attractiveness.

rankingMethod: Regions sorted by normalised weighted score, descending; the regions array is stored in rank order and ranks are sequential 1..n. Ties would be broken by baseDensity and then by evidenceQuality; no tie occurred.

sequencingOverlay.label: ANALYST_JUDGEMENT_SEPARATE_FROM_SCORE
sequencingOverlay.purpose: The weighted score measures absolute attractiveness. Sequencing additionally considers logistics contiguity, shared administration and language, and the cost of serving a second region from the same team.
criteria: Contiguity with the Galician home base and shared regional administration (Xunta / Portos de Galicia)
Single-language operations and the same VAT and consumer regime
Cost and time of installer travel and spare-parts logistics
Avoidance of markets that need a different channel model in the first phase

regions.name: Rías Baixas (Pontevedra coast: Vigo, Baiona, Sanxenxo, Vilagarcía, Marín)
regions.recommendationRationale: Highest absolute attractiveness in the research area and directly reachable from the Galician home base. It should carry the first installation, demonstration-vessel and installer-partnership effort.
evidenceGaps: Regional length and age distribution of moored craft (UNAV-MKT-002 is national/regional; see UNK-MKT-002 and UNK-MKT-003)
Galician charter/rental fleet size by province (UNAV-MKT-007)
Berth counts by individual port rather than provincial aggregate

baseDensity.rationale: More than 4,600 berths across around twenty facilities, about 44% of Galicia's 10,500 documented berths and the densest recreational capacity in the focus area.

demandMomentum.rationale: Pontevedra registered 229 new craft in 2025 against 162 in 2024 (+41.4%), the only coastal Galician province growing and the strongest provincial growth in the region.

addressableMix.rationale: No regional length distribution is published. Scored at the neutral midpoint: marina berths skew larger than the national registration mix (70% of new craft are under 6 m), but nothing regional confirms the size cohort that buys electronics.

commercialOperators.rationale: Active charter and rental activity is documented for the area but not quantified: no disaggregated Galician rental-registration data exist in the ANEN reporting, so the score reflects visible operation, not a measured fleet size.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: August berth occupancy at Sanxenxo reached 100% with a waiting list while July was around 50%, and regional transit traffic was 6,321 vessels in 2024: a strong but concentrated season with a usable shoulder.

channelEcosystem.rationale: At least one Galician company documents a repair/rigging/engine workshop with a physical and online chandlery, and one cooperative advertises on-board electronics installation. Existence is evidenced; density and capacity are not.

evidenceQuality.rationale: Berth capacity, provincial registration flows, transit counts and peak occupancy are all published; fleet counts, length mix and rental fleet are not.

regions.name: Balearic Islands (comparator, not beachhead)
regions.recommendationRationale: Second-highest absolute attractiveness and the best commercial-operator evidence in the set, but deferred: 1,000+ km from the Galician base, a different channel structure (charter brokers, local installers), the most aggressive seasonality and the highest competitive density. Revisit only after the Galician beachhead is proven.
evidenceGaps: Charter-share claim is an excerpt-level reading (CLM-MKT-023)
No charter-fleet count, only registration share

baseDensity.rationale: Baleares led Spanish registrations in 2024 (904) and is part of the Mediterranean capacity pool that holds 67% of Spanish berths; the archipelago's own berth count is not in the retrieved evidence.

addressableMix.rationale: A large-vessel and charter-oriented market with high electronics intensity; the 2024 registration total of 904 shows a bigger addressable pool than any Galician province.

commercialOperators.rationale: 59% of 2024 Balearic registrations were charter-market registrations, the strongest documented commercial-operator signal in the evidence set.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: A very intensive summer season with a long shoulder, but also the most concentrated seasonal pressure; installation labour is scarce in peak months.

channelEcosystem.rationale: A charter-heavy market implies a dense service ecosystem, but no Balearic provider was independently documented in this session.

evidenceQuality.rationale: Registration and charter-share signals exist, but the charter figure was read from a tag-index excerpt and no berth or installer data were retrieved.

regions.name: Catalonia / Barcelona (comparator, not beachhead)
regions.recommendationRationale: Attractive but remote from the Galician base, with a distinct channel structure and no local evidence. It is a later expansion market, not a beachhead.

baseDensity.rationale: Barcelona registered 564 new craft in 2025, the second-largest provincial flow in Spain, and sits in the Mediterranean capacity pool.

demandMomentum.rationale: Barcelona was essentially flat (570 to 564, -1.1%) while Girona fell 26.5%, so provincial momentum within Catalonia is mixed.

addressableMix.rationale: A large Mediterranean cruising and charter market with electronics-intensive craft; supported by registration volume, not by a length distribution.

commercialOperators.rationale: Barcelona recorded 194 rental registrations in 2025, the second-largest charter flow nationally.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: Long Mediterranean season but strong summer concentration; no local occupancy evidence retrieved.

channelEcosystem.rationale: A large market implies channel depth, but no Catalan provider was documented in this session.

evidenceQuality.rationale: Registration and rental series available; nothing on berths, installers or fleet.

regions.name: A Coruña and Costa da Morte (A Coruña, Sada, Ares, Camariñas, Malpica)
regions.recommendationRationale: Ranked fourth on absolute attractiveness but sequenced second: same regional administration, same language and VAT regime, contiguous coastline, and the second-largest Galician registration flow. It can be served by the same team and partners at marginal cost.
evidenceGaps: No installer density; one yard and one cooperative are existence evidence only
Occupancy evidence is a single-summer press report

baseDensity.rationale: A Coruña is the second-largest Galician registration market and its sports ports are documented at close to 90% summer occupancy; provincial berth capacity is not published, so the score is not higher.

demandMomentum.rationale: Registrations fell from 231 in 2024 to 209 in 2025 (-9.5%), in line with the national contraction.

addressableMix.rationale: No regional length distribution; the same national registration proxy is applied as for Rías Baixas.

commercialOperators.rationale: Charter activity is less evident in the retrieved sources than in Rías Baixas, and no regional rental data exist to quantify it.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: Summer occupancy of about 90% with waiting lists for crane and dry use shows a comparable summer peak.

channelEcosystem.rationale: A documented yard/chandlery operates on this coast, plus a naval-electronics services provider in the region; density is unmeasured.

evidenceQuality.rationale: Provincial registration series and local occupancy reporting exist; berth counts by port and length mix do not.

regions.name: Northern Portugal (Viana do Castelo, Póvoa de Varzim, Vila do Conde, Leixões/Matosinhos, Douro/Porto)
regions.recommendationRationale: Sequenced after Rías Baixas and A Coruña despite ranking fifth: it is the only non-Spanish market contiguous with the Galician base, and an 85,000-craft national fleet is the largest documented population in the research area. Entering it needs a Portuguese-language support and installation partner first, which is why it is not phase 1.
evidenceGaps: No regional Portuguese fleet or registration series (UNAV-MKT-002)
Unreconciled national fleet counts (CLM-MKT-015 vs CLM-MKT-016)
No Portuguese installer or chandlery evidence
Undated tourism-portal capacity data; 2019-sourced official port list

baseDensity.rationale: At least 1,088 documented berths across four northern marinas, in a country with about 85,000 registered recreational craft; the national fleet is large but the documented northern marina base is roughly a tenth of Galicia's and incomplete.

demandMomentum.rationale: No regional Portuguese registration series was found; the score is neutral-low because momentum cannot be evidenced either way.

addressableMix.rationale: Marina berth limits (18-20 m maximum length, 2.5-3 m draught) indicate a mid-sized craft population suited to electronics, but no Portuguese length distribution was retrieved.

commercialOperators.rationale: The Douro and Leixões marinas and the official shelter-port list evidence organised recreational boating and operator infrastructure, but no charter-fleet counts were retrieved.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: An Atlantic season comparable to Galicia with an extended autumn shoulder; no Portuguese occupancy data were retrieved, so the score rests on the same climatic argument rather than on measurement.

channelEcosystem.rationale: No Portuguese installer or chandlery was identified in this session; cross-border service logistics are unproven.

evidenceQuality.rationale: National fleet totals exist but are approximate, mutually contradictory (85,000 vs 73,765) and undifferentiated by region; marina pages are undated.

regions.name: Cantabria (Santander, Laredo, Castro Urdiales, San Vicente de la Barquera)
regions.recommendationRationale: Positive momentum but no capacity or channel evidence and far from the Galician base. Watch, do not enter.
evidenceGaps: Whether the 2025 growth is structural or a small-base fluctuation

baseDensity.rationale: No berth count retrieved; the province is small relative to Galicia.

demandMomentum.rationale: Registrations rose from 105 to 138 (+31.4%) in 2025, the strongest growth among the Cantabrian comparators.

addressableMix.rationale: No regional mix data; growth is concentrated in small craft nationally, which argues against a high electronics-relevant share.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: A comparable Cantabrian season; not independently evidenced.

regions.name: Asturias (Gijón, Avilés, Luanco, Ribadesella)
regions.recommendationRationale: Third-region expansion without any local channel evidence; not fundable in this milestone.

baseDensity.rationale: No berth count retrieved for Asturias and no provincial capacity source identified.

demandMomentum.rationale: Registrations fell from 150 in 2024 to 129 in 2025 (-14.0%).

addressableMix.rationale: No regional length or fleet data; scored low because nothing supports a higher judgement.

commercialOperators.rationale: No charter or fleet-operator evidence retrieved.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: A Cantabrian-coast season comparable to northern Galicia; not independently evidenced.

evidenceQuality.rationale: Only the national registration series covers it; no regional market data.

regions.name: Basque Country (Vizcaya, Guipúzcoa)
regions.recommendationRationale: Contracting market and no evidence of a channel; deprioritised.

baseDensity.rationale: No berth count retrieved; Vizcaya and Guipúzcoa registered only 87 new craft between them in 2025.

demandMomentum.rationale: Vizcaya fell from 117 to 53 (-54.7%) and Guipúzcoa from 38 to 34 (-10.5%), the weakest momentum in the comparator set.

regions.name: A Mariña (Lugo: Ribadeo, Viveiro, Celeiro, Foz)
regions.recommendationRationale: Lowest score in the set. Do not allocate first-phase resource; re-assess only if an installer partner appears there or if Lugo growth continues for several years.

baseDensity.rationale: Lugo registers a small fraction of Galician new craft (27 of 465 coastal registrations in 2025) and no berth count for the province was retrieved.

demandMomentum.rationale: Registrations rose from 22 to 27 (+22.7%), a small-base improvement.

addressableMix.rationale: A substantial small-boat and inshore fishing-port character is plausible but unmeasured; no data support a higher score.

commercialOperators.rationale: No charter or fleet-operator evidence was retrieved for this coast.

seasonalityWindow.rationale: An Atlantic season comparable to the rest of Galicia but with thinner visitor-infrastructure evidence.

channelEcosystem.rationale: No installer, yard or chandlery was identified on this coast in this session.

evidenceQuality.rationale: Only the provincial registration series is available; nothing on capacity, mix or channels.

portfolioConclusion.statement: The evidence supports a Galicia-first concentration: Rías Baixas is the only region combining the densest documented berth base with the strongest current registration growth in the focus area; A Coruña is a near-cost second wave; Northern Portugal is the only contiguous non-Spanish market, gated on a Portuguese-language installation partner. The two highest-value Spanish markets (Baleares, Catalonia) are deliberately deferred because their attractiveness does not offset distance, channel difference and seasonality in a first phase.
whatWouldChangeThis: A measured Galician berth length/age distribution showing that most berths hold under-6 m or low-electronics craft would lower Rías Baixas' addressableMix and could make Northern Portugal or A Coruña relatively stronger.
Evidence of a capable installer partner in Northern Portugal would raise that region above A Coruña for phase 2.
A sustained multi-year decline in Pontevedra registrations would remove its momentum advantage, leaving it scored on base density alone.
